recipes.name: Cranberry Apple Stuffed Pork Loin
ingredients_raw: 1 cup chicken flavored dry stuffing mix
salt and black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Coat a roasting pan with cooking spray.
Combine stuffing mix and water in a bowl; stir in apple, cranberries, pecans, and onion. Set aside.

Place pork loin on a flat work surface; trim fat and silverskin. Slice pork loin horizontally through the middle to within ½-inch of the other side, being careful not to cut all the way through. Open the 2 sides; spread them out like an open book. Place pork loin between two sheets of heavy plastic (resealable plastic freezer bags work well). Firmly pound pork loin with the smooth side of a meat mallet to a thickness of ½-inch.

Season pork loin with salt and black pepper; spread reserved stuffing mixture onto cut side of pork loin. Roll pork loin into a firm cylinder; secure with cooking twine. Place in the prepared roasting pan.

Bake in the preheated oven until pork is no longer pink in the center, about 1 hour. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 145 degrees F (63 degrees C). Cover pork loin with two layers of aluminum foil; rest in a warm area for 10 minutes. Remove kitchen twine before slicing and serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Cranberry Apple Stuffed Pork Loin
raw_recipe.description: Apples, toasted pecans, and dried cranberries join dry stuffing mix to create a simple and tasty stuffing for pork loin in this simply elegant recipe.

review.reviewBody: My husband and I really enjoyed this recipe. I did make a few changes - As pork loin can be a little too lean - I brined the pork. I don't usually buy Stovetop stuffing but I did have a bag of Mrs. Cubison's Cubed Stuffing. I made the whole bag of the stuffing - used some in the pork roast and served the rest on the side. I sauted the apples, dried cranberries & pecans as well as adding 2 stalks of celery and half a chopped onion with 1/2 a stick of butter. Used about 1 1/2 cups chicken broth to make up the stuffing. My pork loin was really thick - rather than trying to pound it thin I laid it on it's side as directed and sliced to within a 1/2 inch of the other side, laid it open like a book and then from the center of the roast sliced it both to the right and again to the left - folding back the meat. I ended up with a nice thin rectangle of pork. Spread the stuffing on the pork and rolled it up like a jelly roll. I didn't need to tie mine with kitchen twine. I notice that most recipes for pork roast call for cooking to 160 degrees....which can lead to dried out meat. I cooked mine to 140 - 145. Let rest while I made gravy out of the pan drippings (which were beautiful). Final internal temp. was about 150. Served with baked potatoes, green beans and Cranberry, Apple Apricot sauce. Delish! Thanks for an inspiring recipe.

This is a beautiful recipe! I used this as the base idea for my Christmas dinner with the family... the only difference is I used fresh cranberries for the stuffing (I boiled them in orange juice until they "popped" [approx. 15 minutes - and drain the OJ!]), and instead of using twine and putting the pork in the oven, I wrapped the tenderloins in bacon and grilled them at 350 until the bacon appeared done (approx. 30 to 45 minutes - check with a meat thermometer prior to serving!). This is admittedly a hybrid of 2 recipes I saw (the other was on "Flip my Food with Chef Jeff"), but the preparation of the pork and the stuffing recipe listed here is spot on!

We loved this roast and have decided it will be our Chrismas Holiday meat dish. I followed the recipe with the following tweaks: Brined pork overnight. Did NOT trim fat from loin. Increased water to 3/4 cup. Added 1/4 cup applebutter to apple, cranberry, pecan mixture. Increased chopped onion to 1/3 cup. Sauteed chopped onions along with 1/3 cup diced celery in 1 tablespoon butter to add to stuffing mixture. Stirred stuffing mixture into apple/cranberry/pecan mixture. After spreading the stuffing on the loin and tying in a roll, I quickly browned in 2 tablespoons olive oil; and placed in roasting pan to bake. I removed the roast when the internal temp reached 145 degrees. Covered with tin foil while I made the gravy from the pan drippings. This was probably the best pork loin roast I've ever eaten . It was so moist and had great flavor. It tasted like the best comfort food you could have. I served with sliced oven roasted sweet potatoes, applesauce and sour dough rolls.

I’ve made this twice now, the first time tasted great but I had a hard time rolling the roast so it looked terrible! This time I sautéed the onions and apples before adding them to the stuffing and kept a little bit back in the pan to make a glaze/gravy using apricot preserves and chicken broth. Very yummy. Served with roasted Brussels sprouts

I added celery, and used the whole 12 oz package of Pepperidge Farm stuffing, herb flavored; added more of everything to make extra stuffing mix. Also made a pan gravy from the drippings with flour, water, splash of gravy master, and a healthy splash of white wine, salt, and pepper. reduce by half. Convection roasted to 150 degrees. Seared the meat at 400 degrees for 10 min. reduced temp down to 325 for remainder of cooking. Got a nice golden color around the meat while maintaining a nice moist interior. Not bad for a Wednesday night meal. Wish I had a crowd to please with this winner, but the family most certainly enjoyed this treat!!

I tried to follow the recipe as closely as possible. There are only the two of us and I had several pork tenderloins that needed to be used so I went with that. I removed all visible fat and cut the pork length wise and pounded it to 1/4 inch thick. I had no stuffing mix, never buy it, so I used two cups of cubed ciabatta bread. I soaked the cranberries in hot water to plump them up, recommended by another reviewer. I sauted the apple, onion, pecans and cranberries as well as two ribs of celery. I stuffed the the roast and rolled it, tucking in the edges and tied it with butchers string. I seared the roast in one tbs of oil and finished it off in the oven for approx. 30 mins to a temp of 140. Tented it for 10 minutes. There was far more stuffing than needed, my error, so I buttered an ovenproof dish and baked it. The stuffing adds a whole lot of flavour to the pork and the presentations is so very pretty. I will be making this one again, thanks.

I had some rye bread that was getting stale, so I used that as the basis for homemade stuffing to which I added sauted onion, apple, celery and a link of hot Italian sausage. I used apple juice and butter to moisten the stuffing. I baked half the stuffing as a side dish. I basted the whole roast with apple juice 3 or 4 times while baking (about an hour) I served this with roasted cauliflower, string beans and mashed potato. Somehow, I never remembered to buy cranberries, so they weren't used.

This was tasty... I left out pecans because my kids are not fans of nuts.. *shrug*. I would recommend softening up the apple and onion before mixing it with the stuffing. I had crunchy apple and onion, which wasn't awesome. It would also be real nice with a gravy of some sort... Chicken gravy would even be good... I was thinking of an apple cider reduction... Something.

Excellent recipe!! My family loved it, and they are very picky when it comes to pork. I did do a bit of tweaking but not much. I brined the meat overnight for a juicier roast. I used pork flavored stuffing mix and 2 different apple types (Granny Smith and Gala). I also cooked a tube of ground breakfast sausage and added it to the stuffing (a stuffing tradition in our house). The roast turned out extremely moist and tender. This dish will be repeated many times. Thanks for the recipe.

This has become my go to for a dinner party! Delicious, hard to mess up and beautiful presentation! I use reduced fat craisins. I also deglaze the pan and make a pork gravy on the side which really adds to it.
I left out the pecans and added laughing cow cheese. I used three triangles worth and spread it out before adding other ingredients and rolling. Family loved it.

I never seem to be able to make a recipe as written. this time i had no twine so did no tie it just folded in half, didnt have an apple but I did have a can of pears, then made the recipe . the stuffing was to die for!!!
Delicious! I think resting the roast was very important in retaining it's moisture. Because it can be assembled ahead of time, this will be a good recipe to make for company.
Turned out great, crowd pleaser for my family. I didn't have any apples so I substituted apple sauce and it worked fine.
I used apple juice instead of water and it was amazing!!!

The only mistake I made was not pounding the pork loin down thin enough and therefore was not able to put in all the dressing I wanted to, but the dressing served on the side worked out very well also. I used both Granny Smith and red delicious apples chopped up, along with the cranberries it was an excellent taste. I used no salt at all because of the amount of fat on the pork loin and since I wrapped bacon around the entire loin, that added enough salt and excellent juices to the mix. My girlfriend loved it, and I’m 65 years old! We will certainly have this again. Thanks for the recipe!

I absolutely love this recipe! It’s the perfect dish for family thanksgiving or Christmas dinner. I always have left over stuffing so I put that in a baking dish and throw it in the oven as well. Makes for a perfect additional side.
I think the stuffing need more moisture. I would have liked to have coated the outside with something to give it more flavor.

I pretty much followed the recipe, except I added some extra water because I was afraid the stuffing would be dry. It was absolutely delicious! Tried it later with some pork gravy, but actually preferred it without any. Yum Yum

This was SUPER easy to make and made the whole house smell amazing!
I paired it with roasted baby gold potatoes, chopped onions and apples and cranberries and chopped walnuts. 
There were no leftovers!
